goals: Maintain the curated Fabric-only port of Building But Better 2.0pre4 for Minecraft Java 26.2 without redistributing upstream All Rights Reserved resources.
Preserve the retained building families and their original stateful behavior through an explicit, testable registry and resource-closure contract.
scope: Maintain exactly 160 retained blocks and 161 retained items: eleven wood families, seven stone families, braziers, rope, iron fence, and the Hammer.

Preserve the retained rotation, waterlogging, connectivity, collision, lighting, Hammer, lattice-plant, urn, model, texture, tag, language, recipe, advancement, loot, and drop contracts implemented by legacy source 4ddbd2a7b39cb33653f9ddacf9bca0a419cc500d and finalized at legacy branch head 08cba03bc6b19d43a484e7500ca8b366a254e671.
Stage only the exact audited dependency closure from the hash-verified pristine BBB 2.0pre4 input into ignored generated build output.

exclusions: BBB layers, BBB ladders, the small-stone-block system, Chisel and related removed tools, Pale Oak, and any silently restored registry content.
Rope enhancements, Inventory Bridge Framework changes, Clutter No More changes, or unrelated compatibility implementation.
Upstream models, textures, recipes, data, translations, loot tables, tags, or other All Rights Reserved resources in tracked source, retained artifacts, or redistributed combined development JARs.
Architectury and MidnightLib dependencies removed by the direct Fabric port.
Runtime deployment, Test Slot or Test Instance Manager changes, accepted-stack mutation, dedicated Workbench access, and protected gameplay-profile access during this migration.

Retained Fabric Loom selector from the imported build; the 2026-08-31 verification resolved and reported Fabric Loom 1.17.20.
Exact imported focused-test platform for the 17 curated registry, implementation, and resource-staging tests.
Exact pristine read-only BBB 2.0pre4 input; its curated ARR resource closure may be staged only into ignored generated build output.
